mechanism_claims.claim_text: Fatty-acid anchoring of N36-family peptides increases HIV-1 cell-cell fusion inhibitory potency in the source assay, with stronger effects for longer lipid chains.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: N36 and N36-family lipopeptides in this paper
mechanism_claims.limitations: Functional fusion inhibition evidence; not generalized to antimicrobial MIC endpoints.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hill-coefficient and mutant analyses support a shift from oligomeric soluble N36 behavior toward mainly monomeric lipopeptide inhibition when N36 is membrane-anchored.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: N36, N36M, C16 conjugates, and N36 MUTe,g variants
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper frames this as a mechanistic model supported by specialized curve and mutant analyses, not a resolved structure of the transient fusion intermediate.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NBD-labeling, target/effector-cell binding, and CD experiments provide source evidence for membrane localization and structural context of the anchored peptides.
mechanism_claims.limitations: These assays support localization and secondary-structure context; exact figure-only quantitative binding curves were not converted into new numeric rows.

source_review_notes: Removed automated reference-derived ROS/protein-synthesis placeholder claims from the prior scaffold.
Mechanism claims are bounded to HIV-1 gp41-mediated cell-cell fusion, membrane anchoring/localization, and N36-family inhibitory mode evidence present in the paper.
